column1: # The autonomy plan — what the loop works on, in order, one item per cycle.
# One row: id <tab> spec <tab> brief(- = the dispatcher's own brief) <tab> title <tab> verify(cmd;cmd) <tab> commit paths(a;b) <tab> gate(1|0)
# The id column MUST be unique — state.json is keyed by it, so a second row reusing an id silently inherits the
# first row's status and is never dispatched. Measured 2026-10-14: rows A20/151 (done) and A20/152 (queued, its spec
# and brief already committed) both said A20, so the finished 151 marked the queued 152 done and ~5 h of cycles
# reported "queue empty" with work sitting in the queue. state.py now refuses a duplicate id, and the cycle prints
# OUTCOME=plan-error instead of pretending the queue is empty.
# The verify column MUST be the spec's own Exit Criteria, copied verbatim — same commands, same sense.
# A paraphrased criterion is one nobody agreed to, and it re-fails a correct worker for ever. Measured
# 2026-10-13: A8 failed twice on a hand-written `! grep -q Dockerfile`, STRICTER than spec 141's
# "no Docker line without systemd", against a doc that was right (all four criteria rc=0, every number
# in it re-measured exact). Align the row, not the doc.
# The opposite direction is worse: a criterion REWRITTEN WEAKER so an item can pass. Spec 141's criterion 4
# was swapped for `grep -qi systemd` in fd62a20 - never needed (the original runs rc=0 on the committed
# tree) and reverted; nobody edits a criterion weaker, and a worker that cannot meet one stops and says so.
# A9/A11/A12 now carry their specs' criteria in full too: a row that drops one is a gate nobody sees.
# Every row traces to a measured finding, and the finding's own gate is the verify list. Order is
# cheapest-and-most-decisive first, so the machinery proves itself on a 10-line item before it is
# trusted with a defect fix. Nothing here is invented: the source of each row is named.
